OS-1.name: Reliability-Verified Air Purifiers (extended-life guarantee + real-time self-diagnostic)
OS-1.usage_context: Any household buying a purifier as a health/allergy necessity, not a discretionary gadget
OS-1.friction: Unit silently 'stops working' or 'dies' well before its expected life, with no warning and often outside a short return window - a complaint pattern visible across brands and across the full 2004-2023 span of this real corpus, meaning it has never been solved industry-wide
OS-1.enabling_trend: TC-R08 (Matter Air Quality Sensor cluster - the same connectivity layer could carry a self-diagnostic/runtime health signal); TC-R02 (ENERGY STAR IEF/CADR measurement already requires performance verification, a template for an ongoing performance-verified claim)
OS-1.evidence: src/real/taxonomy_real.py theme 'reliability', polarity-gated real-text classification, n=166 reviews

OS-2.name: Whisper-Quiet Night Mode
OS-2.enabling_trend: TC-R11 (Dyson formaldehyde-sensor press release, tangential); no real trend document in this corpus directly addresses acoustic engineering

OS-3.name: Smart/Connected Feature Expansion (app control, voice assistant)
OS-3.friction: Presumed friction with manual app/physical control
OS-3.enabling_trend: TC-R08 (Matter Air Quality Sensor device type), TC-R07 (Versuni's own AI-purifier launch)
OS-3.evidence: keyword search across all 10529 real reviews: 107 matches (1.016%); reviews that DO mention connectivity skew POSITIVE (feature praise, not complaint) on manual inspection

verdict.recommended_name: Reliability-Verified Air Purifiers (extended-life guarantee + real-time self-diagnostic)
verdict.why: Real data presents a genuine Pareto trade-off, not a dominant winner: Noise (OS-2) reaches more reviews (3.5% vs 1.58%) and touches higher-price-exposure products ($84,016 vs $26,358), but its satisfaction hit is the mildest of any real theme (-0.571 stars). Reliability (OS-1) reaches fewer reviews but its satisfaction hit is severe (-2.223 stars, close to the worst in the whole real taxonomy) and, unlike noise, a reliability failure typically ends the customer relationship outright (no repeat purchase, no consumable/filter revenue at all afterward) rather than just annoying a buyer who keeps the unit. That asymmetry - shallow-but-broad vs. severe-and-relationship-ending - is the explicit judgment call this recommendation rests on, not a formula: see 'most sensitive assumption' below.

killed.name: Whisper-Quiet Night Mode
killed.killing_metric: CSAT Impact = -0.571 stars - the SHALLOWEST satisfaction hit of any theme in the real taxonomy, despite the highest prevalence
killed.reason: Noise is the most-mentioned real friction, but solving it moves satisfaction the least. On the same real evidence, a euro spent on quieting the motor buys less improvement in the metric that actually predicts whether a buyer stays a customer than the same euro spent on reliability. 'Mentioned often' and 'worth fixing first' are not the same claim, and this real corpus is where that distinction is visible.

killed.name: Smart/Connected Feature Expansion (app control, voice assistant)
killed.killing_metric: Friction Prevalence % = 1.016% (107 of 10529 reviews) - and on manual inspection, most of those mentions are FEATURE PRAISE, not complaints
killed.reason: Unlike the earlier synthetic-fixture version of this exercise, connectivity mentions are not literally zero in real data (~1%) - but they are the smallest of the three real candidates AND skew positive when they do appear (e.g., 'It is incredibly powerful and [connectivity feature]... impressed with it'). There is no real friction signal here to build a roadmap bet on, only a feature people occasionally mention liking.

verdict.sensitivity: The recommendation is most sensitive to the judgment call in 'why' above: that a severe-but-narrower friction (reliability) is worth prioritizing over a shallow-but-broader one (noise). A different but equally defensible business judgment - reach matters more than depth, because a mildly annoyed majority still drives more aggregate churn than a severely annoyed minority - would flip this to OS-2. This is a genuine, stated either-way call; it is not resolved by the data alone.
verdict.first_experiment_os1: Cross-reference the real review corpus's product-level failure mentions ('stopped working', 'died', 'never worked') against each real product's rating_number (a rough popularity proxy) to identify whether failure reports cluster in specific brands/price tiers or are evenly distributed - if evenly distributed, this is a category-wide manufacturing/QA opportunity; if clustered, it may instead argue for a narrower positioning bet against the worst-performing competitors specifically.
verdict.abandon_signal_os1: If the failure-mention cross-reference above shows reliability complaints concentrated in 2-3 specific older/discontinued products rather than spread across the category, treat this as a solved-or-solving problem rather than a live opportunity, and abandon.

market_scenario.note: The Q6 scores above do not depend on category CAGR at all - they are built entirely from review-level prevalence/CSAT/price-exposure, so this scenario flag changes the category-sizing narrative in Q5/insight_pack but changes NOTHING in this file's scores or verdict. Run with --market-scenario=imarc to see this confirmed live.
